title: Regularity of a ring map is local on the target
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ be a ring map of commutative rings with $\Lambda$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ with $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ write $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, for the induced map of localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The following are equivalent: (1) $\varphi$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; (2) $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; (3) $\varphi_{\mathfrak m'}:R_{\mathfrak m}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak m'}$ is regular for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$ (a prime ideal of $R$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local, line 10390); its proof cites Algebra Definition 00OD (regular ring: all local rings regular) and Algebra Lemma 00HT (lemma-flat-localization)
